name: Emerging-market stress
summary: Bank Indonesia raised rates to 6% on 18 Nov to support the rupiah near record lows; no EM default or IMF rescue
state: Bank Indonesia unexpectedly raised its benchmark rate by 0.25 points to 6% on 18 Nov after stepping up intervention, following a record low near 18,290 per dollar on 17 Nov; the rupiah is down about 9% in 2026 (Trading Economics). Pressure came from a strong dollar, Fed rate-rise bets, fund outflows and political uncertainty (The Jakarta Post). The currency has not fallen 10% in a month, and no major emerging economy in default, under capital controls or seeking emergency IMF support was found as of 20 Nov.
for_you: A strong dollar raises costs for emerging economies that borrow or import in dollars, and for firms and travellers dealing in their currencies.
rubric_hit: No major EM with >10% monthly currency fall, default or IMF rescue: Normal; rupiah pressure noted

sources.title: Trading Economics — Rupiah recovers but heads for weekly losses
The Jakarta Post — Rupiah touches new low on Fed hike bets, politics

why: Energy-importing and heavily indebted emerging economies crack first in oil shocks and strong-dollar periods, with knock-on defaults and unrest.
drivers: Oil and food import bills, dollar strength, FX reserves, debt maturities, IMF programmes.

rubric.alert: A sovereign default or capital controls in a major emerging economy, or several in crisis at once.
rubric.watch: A major emerging economy's currency falls more than 10% in a month, its reserves fall fast, or it seeks emergency IMF support.
rubric.normal: No major emerging economy in acute currency or debt distress.
